candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is vertebral hemangioma, which is the primary pathological entity (expansile bony lesion of T1 with epidural extension). Spinal cord compression at T1-T3 describes the neurological consequence/complication of that lesion, not the etiological diagnosis requested. The candidate also misidentifies the anatomical level as T1-T3 rather than centered at T1.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Spinal cord compression is the clinical complication/manifestation caused by the vertebral hemangioma, not the underlying diagnosis itself

case_quality_flags: Vertebral hemangioma is a reasonable but not definitive diagnosis without histopathology; the case notes tissue diagnosis was pending at time of question

Aggressive vertebral hemangioma with epidural extension is a rare presentation; differential includes metastatic disease, primary bone tumor, and lymphoma, all of which were not excluded pre-operatively
